en.title: Witcher 3 Remaster Confirmed to Run Smoothly on Steam Deck
en.summary: Good news for portable Geralt fans: CD Projekt Red has confirmed that The Witcher 3 Remastered will perform admirably on the Steam Deck. Prepare for a visually enhanced, yet consistently playable, monster-slaying experience on Valve's handheld.
en.body:
The highly anticipated remaster of **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt** is bringing its visually stunning world and extensive content to a new generation of hardware, but a key question has loomed for many: how will it perform on the portable **Steam Deck**? CD Projekt Red’s executive producer of external projects, **Jakub Kutrzuba**, has now offered a reassuring answer, speaking to PC Gamer. He stated that the remaster is designed to run just as well as the original on the **Steam Deck**, while looking significantly better.

Kutrzuba explained that the new rendering engine brings substantial optimization improvements. "When it comes to Steam Deck, based on what we see, the game will work the same way, but look much much better," he said. "Because from one side we are bringing all these improvements, we are bringing new content, we are upgrading the assets, but [we also have] the new rendering features." These advancements allow the game to present a more beautiful image without demanding more from the hardware, a benefit also expected for the upcoming **Nintendo Switch 2**. This focus on efficient performance echoes lessons learned from the challenging launch of **Cyberpunk 2077**, with CD Projekt Red aiming for a polished experience across platforms.

## Geralt on the Go

This news will come as a significant relief to the **Steam Deck** community, who have been eagerly anticipating the remaster. While the original **The Witcher 3** already runs well on the handheld, often achieving stable frame rates with a mix of medium and high settings, there were concerns that the graphical overhaul and new content might introduce performance issues. Early reports from the community suggest that the original version can achieve around 40-45 FPS with specific settings and power management, offering a solid few hours of gameplay on a single charge. The confirmation from CD Projekt Red that the remaster will maintain this level of performance, while enhancing the visual fidelity, means players can look forward to experiencing **The Witcher 3's** rich narrative and vast open world on their **Steam Deck** without compromising on the gameplay experience.

## Community Concerns and Future Updates

Despite the positive performance outlook for the **Steam Deck**, some players still have lingering questions. Concerns about the transferability of existing save files to the remastered version remain, as does the potential impact on the thriving modding scene for **The Witcher 3**. Many are also curious about the precise increase in system requirements for PC players. While CD Projekt Red has historically been responsive to community feedback, details on these specific issues have not yet been announced. Players are eager to know if their current setups, including older GPUs like the **1660 Ti**, will be able to handle the enhanced visuals. As the release date approaches, more information is expected to be shared regarding these important player considerations.

## What's Next

The **Witcher 3 Remastered** is set to launch soon, with details regarding its precise release date on PC and consoles expected imminently. Players are advised to keep an eye on official channels for further announcements.

content_raw: As is the case with a lot of older games (I regret to inform you that The Witcher 3 is 11 years old) that get the remaster treatment, there's been some anxiety over whether The Witcher 3 Remastered will run properly on the Steam Deck—especially given it'll be a free update . It's always frustrating when some new glossy graphics pack messes with your hardware. Well, fear not—speaking to PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens ahead of Gamescom 2026 , CD Projekt Red's executive producer of external projects Jakub Kutrzuba has told us that The Witcher 3 Remastered will run just as well on your Steam Deck, thanks to general optimisation improvements with the new rendering engine. "When it comes to Steam Deck, based on what we see, the game will work the same way, but look much much better. Because from one side we are bringing all these improvements, we are bringing new content, we are upgrading the assets, but [we also have] the new rendering features." These features, Kutrzuba says, give the game more hardware budget for all those fancy spangled new assets and textures: "With the newer rendering engine, many of the systems just work faster. So we are just capable of showing a more beautiful image with the same cost, and this is also the case for the Nintendo Switch 2, which is coming together with the Remaster as well." So, no, the Remaster isn't some monster that'll eat all of your Steam Deck's RAM. In general, CD Projekt seems to've learned its lesson after the horror show of Cyberpunk 2077, with its developers boasting solid performance out of The Witcher 4 , as well. You'll be able to engage in some cosy, lo-fi monster slaying in the windswept, freshly-beautified White Orchard without fretting about frame drops. Which is good, because given Wolens' stellar impression of the Remaster's graphical update , you'll want to.
